name: The Astronomer’s Vigil
image_style: A richly detailed 16th-century illuminated-manuscript-inspired digital gouache, combining precise medieval marginal ornament, subdued tempera textures, parchment grain, and crisp cinematic landscape depth. The mood is solemn, contemplative, gently absurd, and historically grounded. Use an unusual palette of deep aubergine, oxidized teal, smoked ivory, muted saffron, and restrained vermilion, with fine ink contours and sparse gilded accents. Keep the upper edge spacious and visually quiet, with one calm area suitable for desktop widgets; no lettering, borders, logos, or interface elements.
scene: A moonlit Crusader-era observatory built into the roof of a remote stone monastery, rendered with reverence: below, a small Romanesque chapel and cloister sit peacefully among dark cypress, wind-bent juniper, and snow-dusted hills; a stone sundial, brass astrolabe, star charts without readable marks, and carefully arranged astronomical instruments occupy the terrace. Space Ghost stands respectfully beside the astrolabe, muscular white costume immaculate, black hood and mask, yellow cape hanging still, red power bands visible, studying the heavens with comically absolute seriousness as though appointed guardian of the observatory. He is clearly an out-of-place visitor, never holy or devotional, and no one worships or venerates him. A faint meteor trail and an enormous quiet violet sky create the visual joke and leave the upper-left sky calm for desktop widgets. Landscape composition, exactly one striking 16:10 wallpaper, no words or lettering.
